recipes.name: Greek Turkey Meatballs with Tzatziki, Lemon-Herb Rice & Pickled Onions
recipes.blurb: Juicy turkey meatballs packed with grated zucchini, garlic, red onion, mint, parsley and oregano, baked on sheet pans. Serve them over lemon-herb rice made from Wednesday's batch or tucked into warm pitas, with cool garlicky tzatziki, cucumber, tomato, feta and Monday's pickled onions. Chosen for the Butterball 48-oz ground turkey tray at $10.99, about $3.66/lb.

ingredients.group: Meatballs (recipe scaled 2.4x to the full 3 lb tray)
items: 2 1/2 cups grated zucchini, squeezed very dry (the ~12 oz held back Tuesday)
1/3 cup chopped fresh oregano (or 2 tsp dried)
16 oz plain Greek yogurt (2% or whole; thick enough that you can skip the recipe's straining)
1 hot house cucumber, peeled, seeded, grated and squeezed dry (about 2 cups)
2 Tbsp sliced green-onion tops (in place of the recipe's chives, saved from Wednesday)
1 lb tomatoes on the vine, chopped

directions: TZATZIKI FIRST: grate the cucumber, salt it lightly, and squeeze it hard in a clean towel. Stir it into the yogurt with the garlic, lemon juice, dill, green-onion tops, salt and pepper. Refrigerate at least 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Line 2 sheet pans with parchment or spray them with oil.

Wet the bread with water, squeeze out the excess, and tear it into small pieces in a large bowl. Add the turkey, eggs, zucchini, breadcrumbs, garlic, grated onion, mint, parsley, oregano, salt and pepper. Mix gently with your hands until just combined.
Form 1/4-cup portions and flatten them slightly (about 32-36). Refrigerate them 10-15 min if you have time; they hold their shape better.
Bake 20-25 min until cooked through (165°F), rotating the pans halfway. This is the recipe's oven method. Its stovetop method (very low heat, 5-6 min per side) is too slow for 3 lb.

Rice: warm Wednesday's rice in a large covered skillet with the olive oil and a splash of water, 5 min, until steaming. Off the heat, stir in the lemon zest and juice, the parsley, the mint and a pinch of salt.
Slice the cucumber, chop the tomatoes, crumble the feta and warm the pitas.
Build bowls or pitas: rice, meatballs, a big spoon of tzatziki, cucumber-tomato, pickled onions and feta. Paul's share is about 12 oz of turkey (~65 g protein). Leftover meatballs are Friday lunches.

recipes.name: Lemon Chicken Piccata with Whole-Wheat Spaghetti & Roasted Squash
recipes.blurb: Thin chicken cutlets dusted in flour and pan-fried golden in olive oil and butter, then glossed with a lemon, caper, shallot and white wine sauce. Extra sauce dresses whole-wheat spaghetti, and roasted yellow squash and zucchini go alongside. Chosen for Perdue thin-sliced chicken breasts, BOGO FREE: both packs go in tonight.

ingredients.group: Chicken (recipe scaled 1.25x; Perdue cutlets are already thin)
items: 2 packs Perdue thin-sliced chicken breasts, about 2 1/2 lb (BOGO)

ingredients.group: Piccata sauce (1.5x, so there's enough for the pasta)
items: 1/2 cup dry white wine (the rest of Monday's bottle)
1/3 cup chopped parsley, plus more to garnish
1 tray (24 oz) yellow squash + about half the zucchini tray, cut into half-moons

directions: Heat the oven to 425°F and put a pot of salted water on to boil.
Toss the squash and zucchini with the olive oil, salt and pepper on a sheet pan. Roast 20-25 min until the edges brown. KEEP 2 small zucchini (~12 oz) raw for Thursday.
Pat the cutlets dry. If any piece is thicker than 1/2 inch, slice it in half horizontally. Season both sides with salt and pepper and dredge lightly in the flour.

Heat 1 1/2 Tbsp oil and 1 1/2 Tbsp butter in a large heavy skillet over medium to medium-high heat. Cook the cutlets in a single layer, 2-3 min per side, until golden and cooked through (165°F). Move them to a plate. Repeat with the rest of the oil and cooking butter; it takes 2-3 batches.
Meanwhile, cook the spaghetti according to the package. Save 1 cup of pasta water before draining.
Lower the heat to medium-low. Cook the shallots in the same skillet 2-3 min until lightly caramelized. Add the wine and broth, raise the heat to medium, and simmer 3-4 min until reduced by half.
Turn the heat to low. Stir in the lemon zest and juice, the capers, and the 3 Tbsp cold butter. Season to taste, then stir in the parsley.

Toss the drained spaghetti with about a third of the sauce and a splash of pasta water. Spoon the rest of the sauce over the chicken. Squeeze lemon over the squash. Pass the Parmesan. Paul's share is about 10 oz of chicken (~65 g protein).

recipes.name: Seared Pork Shoulder Steaks with Garlic-Wine Pan Sauce, Roasted Baby Golds & Cucumber-Tomato Salad
recipes.blurb: Thick pork shoulder steaks, slow-baked and then hard-seared in cast iron, finished with a garlic, scallion, white wine and butter pan sauce. Served with crispy roasted baby gold potatoes and a sharp cucumber-tomato salad with quick-pickled red onions. Chosen for this week's anchor deal: Publix pork shoulder blade steaks, BOGO FREE.

ingredients.group: Pork steaks (recipe scaled 1.5x; bone-in shoulder steaks)
items: 2 packs Publix pork shoulder blade steaks, about 4 lb bone-in total, 3/4 to 1 inch thick (BOGO)
6 green onions, thinly sliced (the rest of the bunch goes to Wednesday)
1 1/2 cups dry white wine (or low-sodium chicken broth). Save the rest of the bottle for Tuesday.
2 bags (24 oz each) baby gold potatoes, halved

ingredients.group: Pickled onions (DOUBLE: half is Thursday's) + salad
items: 1 lb tomatoes on the vine, chunked (the other pound is Thursday's)

directions: 4:30 PM: PICKLE THE ONIONS. Put both sliced red onions in a quart jar with the vinegar, hot water, sugar and salt. Shake and leave it on the counter. Half the jar is Thursday's, so make the full batch.

Heat the oven to 425°F. Pat the pork steaks dry and season all over with the salt and pepper. Set them on a wire rack over a parchment-lined sheet pan and leave them at room temperature for 30 minutes.

Meanwhile, toss the halved potatoes with the olive oil, salt and pepper on a second sheet pan. Roast 25-30 min, tossing once, until browned. Pull them out, tent with foil, and drop the oven to 275°F (prop the door open for 2-3 min).

Bake the pork at 275°F until the thickest part reads 120-125°F, 25-35 min. Bone-in thick steaks run longer than the recipe's 20-25 min. Pull any that finish early. Slide the potatoes onto the lower rack for the last 10 min to rewarm.
Salad: toss the cucumber and tomatoes with the olive oil, a pinch of salt, a splash of the pickling liquid, a big forkful of pickled onions and the parsley.

Heat 1 Tbsp oil in a cast-iron skillet over medium-high until it's smoking. Sear the steaks 2 at a time without moving them, about 3 min, until crusted. Flip and cook 2-3 min more, to 145°F. Add oil between batches. Rest under foil for 5 min.

Sauce: lower the heat to medium. Add the green onions and garlic and cook 30 seconds. Add the wine and soy sauce, scraping up the browned bits. Simmer until reduced by a bit more than half, about 5-6 min. Off the heat, stir in the butter.
Spoon the sauce over the steaks. Serve with the potatoes and salad. Shoulder steaks are fatty and very forgiving, so they're hard to overcook. Paul gets the biggest steak (about 50 g protein).

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Sesame-Ginger Shrimp & Broccoli over Jasmine Rice
recipes.blurb: Broccoli roasted in a soy, rice vinegar, honey, garlic and ginger glaze until the edges char. Jumbo shrimp go onto the pan for the last 5 minutes, then everything gets sesame seeds and scallions and goes over jasmine rice. No cornstarch in this sauce, which is why this recipe won over the stir-fry versions. Chosen for Publix peeled & deveined jumbo white shrimp, 24-oz bags at $14.99.

ingredients.group: Shrimp and broccoli (recipe doubled, plus extra shrimp; two sheet pans)
items: 3 lb jumbo raw shrimp, peeled and deveined (2 frozen 24-oz bags, thawed)
3 bunches broccoli, cut into florets (about 10 cups)
1/2 cup sliced green onions (the rest of Monday's bunch + the second bunch)
1/4 tsp red pepper flakes (more at the table)
4 1/2 cups dry jasmine rice + water per the package

directions: TUESDAY NIGHT: move both bags of shrimp to the fridge to thaw. If you forget, put them in a sealed bag in cold water for 15-20 min on Wednesday.
Cook all 4 1/2 cups of rice (use a big pot or two batches). That's three times what tonight needs: about half is Thursday's.
Heat the oven to 400°F. Line two rimmed sheet pans with foil and oil them lightly. Divide the florets between the pans.

Whisk the soy sauce, rice vinegar, olive oil, honey, water, garlic, ginger and pepper flakes. Drizzle half over the broccoli and toss. Roast 20-22 min, tossing and swapping the pans halfway, until tender.
Pat the shrimp dry. Add them to the pans, pour half of the remaining sauce over, toss, and spread in an even layer. Roast 5-6 min, just until pink and opaque. Don't let them go longer.
Sprinkle with the sesame seeds and green onions. Serve over rice with the last of the sauce drizzled on top. Sriracha or pepper flakes on the side for heat.

BEFORE YOU SIT DOWN: spread about 5 cups of the leftover rice on a plate or sheet to cool fast, then refrigerate it covered. That's Thursday's lemon-herb rice. Paul's share is about 3/4 lb of shrimp (~70 g protein).

recipes.name: Chicken Shawarma Wraps with Lemon Yogurt Sauce
recipes.blurb: Thin chicken cutlets marinated in cardamom, cumin, coriander, smoked paprika and lemon, seared hard until charred. They're wrapped in warm pita with garlicky lemon yogurt, spinach, Campari tomatoes, cucumber, red onion and feta. Chosen for this week's anchor deal: Springer Mountain Farms chicken breasts, BOGO FREE.

ingredients.group: Chicken and marinade (scaled 1.5x and switched from thighs to breasts, per the recipe's own note)
items: 3 lb boneless skinless chicken breasts (the first Springer pack)
1/2 tsp cayenne (the recipe's 1 1/2 tsp, dialed down for the kids; hot sauce on the side)

ingredients.group: Lemon yogurt sauce (TRIPLE batch: 1 cup is Tuesday's)
items: 3/4 tsp kosher salt, pinch of pepper
1 bag (6 oz) baby spinach (the other bag is Wednesday's)
1 pkg Campari tomatoes, sliced (the other pack is Tuesday's)
1 pkg (4 oz) crumbled feta (the other is Tuesday's)

directions: MORNING (or Sunday night): cut each chicken breast in half horizontally into thin steaks no thicker than 1/2 inch (1 cm). Pound any thick spots lightly.

Mix the garlic, coriander, cumin, cardamom, cayenne, paprika, salt, pepper, lemon juice and olive oil in a large zip-top bag. Add the chicken, massage to coat, and refrigerate at least 3 hours and up to 24.

Make the sauce: stir together the yogurt, grated garlic, lemon juice, olive oil, salt and pepper. Thin with a spoonful of water if it's stiff. ↻ Spoon 1 CUP into a jar, label it TUESDAY and refrigerate it. It keeps 3 days. Let the rest sit at least 20 minutes.
Slice the tomatoes, cucumber and red onion. Set out the spinach, feta and hot sauce.

Heat a large skillet or grill pan on HIGH with a thin slick of oil. Cook the chicken in batches without crowding, about 2 minutes per side, until deeply golden and cooked through (165°F). Thin breast cutlets dry out fast, so don't go longer.
Rest the chicken 5 minutes, then slice into strips.
Warm the pitas in a dry skillet, or wrapped in foil in a 300°F oven for 10 minutes.
Build the wraps: a swipe of yogurt sauce, spinach, tomato, cucumber, onion, chicken, then feta. Hot sauce on the side. Plan on 3 wraps for Paul.

recipes.name: Pork Chops with Apples & Onions, Sage Rice & Roasted Broccoli
recipes.blurb: Flour-dusted pork chops seared golden, then simmered in a buttery Dijon pan sauce with sliced apples, onions and fresh sage. They're served over Wednesday's rice, reheated with butter and sage, with charred lemony broccoli. Chosen for Publix assorted pork loin chops, BOGO FREE (8 per pack: cook one, freeze one), with Sweetango apples, also BOGO.

ingredients.group: Pork and apples (chops doubled to 8, sauce scaled 1.5x)
items: 8 pork loin chops, at least 3/4 inch thick (one BOGO pack; freeze the free one)
1 1/2 tsp kosher salt, divided; 3/4 tsp black pepper, divided
3 Sweetango apples, thinly sliced, peels on
1 1/2 Tbsp chopped fresh sage, plus more to serve
Wednesday's reserved rice + 1 Tbsp butter + 1 tsp chopped sage
1 bunch broccoli, cut into florets, + 2 Tbsp olive oil + 1/2 tsp salt + 1 lemon

directions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the broccoli with 2 Tbsp olive oil and 1/2 tsp salt on a sheet pan and roast 18-22 minutes, until the edges char. It's hands-off while you do the chops.
Pat the chops dry. In a shallow dish, whisk the flour with 3/4 tsp salt and a scant 1/2 tsp pepper.

Heat 1 1/2 Tbsp oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high. Dredge 4 chops in the flour, shake off the excess, and sear 2-3 minutes per side until browned but not cooked through. Move them to a plate. Repeat with the remaining oil and chops.
Lower the heat to medium-low. Melt the butter, then add the apples, onions and the remaining salt and pepper. Cook 5 minutes, stirring often, until the apples just turn tender. Stir in the Dijon.
Slowly pour in the broth, stirring and scraping up the browned bits. Simmer 3 minutes.
Stir in the sage. Return the chops and their juices to the pan, overlapping is fine, and simmer until they reach 135°F, 2-5 minutes. Check boneless or thin chops early. Rest 5 minutes off the heat.
Meanwhile, reheat Wednesday's rice: microwave it covered with 2 Tbsp water for 3-4 minutes, stirring halfway. Stir in 1 Tbsp butter, 1 tsp chopped sage and a pinch of salt.
Squeeze the lemon over the broccoli. Serve the chops over the rice, spooning the apples, onions and pan sauce on top, with broccoli alongside. 2 chops for Paul.

recipes.name: Steak Fajitas with Lime-Cilantro Crema & Campari Pico
recipes.blurb: Cumin, coriander and lime-zest rubbed sirloin seared in cast iron and sliced thin. It comes with caramelized peppers and onions, warm flour tortillas, a fresh tomato pico, feta and Monday's yogurt sauce turned into a lime crema. Chosen for Publix boneless top sirloin at $6.99/lb, the best-value steak in the ad, swapped in for the recipe's flank ($15.99/lb this week).

ingredients.group: Steak and marinade (scaled from 1 1/2 lb to 2 1/2 lb)
items: 2 1/2 lb boneless top sirloin steak, about 1 inch thick
3 1/2 tsp ground cumin (plus 3/4 tsp for the vegetables)
1 1/2 tsp chili powder (plus 3/4 tsp for the vegetables)
1/2 tsp chipotle chile powder (the recipe uses more; kept mild for the kids)
1 1/2 tsp kosher salt (plus 3/4 tsp for the vegetables)
3 limes: zest and juice (about 1/3 cup juice)
2 Tbsp olive oil for the marinade + 2 Tbsp for cooking
4 bell peppers, cut into 1/4-inch strips (the other 2 are Wednesday's)
2 sweet onions, halved and cut into 1/4-inch strips
1 cup reserved yogurt sauce from Monday + juice of 1 lime + 2 Tbsp chopped cilantro
1 pkg Campari tomatoes, diced, + 1/4 sweet onion, minced, + 1/4 cup cilantro + juice of 1 lime + salt
1 lime in wedges; hot sauce or pickled jalapeños on the side

directions: Mix 3 1/2 tsp cumin, 1 1/2 tsp chili powder, the chipotle powder, coriander and 1 1/2 tsp salt in a small bowl. Zest the 3 limes straight into it and stir.
Make shallow diagonal cuts across the top of the steak, then repeat the other way for a crosshatch. Do both sides. Rub the spice mix all over and put the steak in a sturdy zip-top bag.

In the same bowl, whisk the juice of those 3 limes, 2 Tbsp olive oil, the Worcestershire and the honey. Pour it into the bag, seal, and turn to coat. Rest at room temperature 30-60 minutes, turning once or twice.

Meanwhile: stir the juice of 1 lime and 2 Tbsp cilantro into Monday's reserved cup of yogurt sauce (that's the crema). Toss the diced tomatoes, minced onion, 1/4 cup cilantro, juice of 1 lime and a pinch of salt (that's the pico).
Heat the oven to 300°F and put the tortillas in, wrapped in foil.

Remove the steak, shake off the marinade and pat it COMPLETELY dry. Heat 1 Tbsp oil in your largest cast-iron skillet over medium-high. Sear 4-6 minutes per side to 135°F for medium-rare (sirloin is leaner than the recipe's flank, so pull it a little earlier than the 140°F it gives). Cook in two batches if it won't fit flat. Rest 10 minutes under foil, then slice thin across the grain.
Add the remaining 1 Tbsp oil to the same skillet. Add the peppers and onions and sauté, stirring often, until they soften and the onions start to turn golden, about 8 minutes.
Lower to medium and add 3/4 tsp each of cumin, chili powder and salt. Cook 6-8 minutes more, until soft and caramelized. Stir in the garlic for 30 seconds and take it off the heat.

Pile the steak on a platter with its board juices poured over, with the vegetables alongside. Serve with tortillas, crema, pico, feta, avocado, lime wedges and heat on the side. Plan on 4-5 fajitas for Paul.

recipes.name: Thai Red Curry Chicken with Broccoli & Spinach
recipes.blurb: Seared chicken baked in a red-curry coconut sauce with peppers, onion, ginger and broccoli. Spinach and lime go in at the end, and it's served over jasmine rice with cilantro. Uses the second (free) pack of this week's Springer Mountain Farms chicken breast BOGO, plus coconut milk 2 for $7 and the jasmine rice BOGO.

ingredients.group: Curry (scaled from 1 1/2 lb to 2 1/2 lb chicken)
items: 2 1/2 lb boneless skinless chicken breasts (the free Springer pack)
3/4 tsp kosher salt, 3/4 tsp black pepper
1 sweet onion, thinly sliced (stands in for the recipe's leek so the onion bag gets used up)
3 Tbsp Thai Kitchen red curry paste (mild; sriracha on the side for more)
1 bunch broccoli, cut into bite-size florets (added; the other bunch is Thursday's)
Juice of 1 lime, plus 1 in wedges (added for brightness)

directions: Start the rice: rinse 4 cups of jasmine rice and cook it per the package (rice cooker or pot). ↻ This is a DOUBLE batch, and half is Thursday's.
Heat the oven to 375°F. Halve any thick chicken breasts horizontally so they cook evenly, cut them into large chunks, pat dry, and season with the salt and pepper.
Heat the coconut oil in your largest ovenproof skillet (12-inch or bigger) over medium-high. Sear the chicken in batches until golden on both sides, not cooked through, then move it to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium-low. Add the peppers, onion, garlic and ginger and cook 2 minutes, until slightly softened.

Stir in the curry paste and cook 5 minutes, stirring often. Add a splash of coconut milk if it sticks. Slowly pour in the coconut milk, stirring as you go. Stir in the broccoli, then nestle the chicken and its juices back in. If the skillet is overfull, move everything to a 9x13 baking dish.
Bake 25 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F.
Stir in the spinach until it wilts, then squeeze in the juice of 1 lime and taste for salt. Scatter the cilantro on top.
Serve over rice with lime wedges and sriracha on the side. ↻ Spread the second half of the rice on a sheet pan to cool for 15 minutes, then cover and refrigerate it for Thursday.

recipes.name: Garlic Shrimp & Orzo Skillet
recipes.blurb: One pan, 35 minutes, no sides needed. The orzo cooks risotto-style right in the broth.

items: 1.5 lb large shrimp, peeled, deveined, tails off
1/3 cup sun-dried tomatoes, chopped (reserve the oil)
1 lemon, sliced into wheels and seeded
1/2 cup frozen spinach, rinsed and squeezed dry
1.5 Tbsp sun-dried tomato oil or olive oil
1/4 tsp chili flakes, 3/4 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 1/4 tsp paprika

directions: Prep everything first — slice the lemon, mince the garlic, dice the onion, chop the sun-dried tomatoes. This moves fast once the pan is hot.
Pat the shrimp thoroughly dry, then toss with chili flakes, salt, pepper and paprika.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium-high. Cook the onion 4-6 minutes until softened.

Add the oil, then the shrimp in a single even layer. Cook 2-3 minutes per side, just until pink. Pull them out to a clean plate immediately — they finish cooking later, and rubbery shrimp is the only way to lose here.
Add orzo, garlic and sun-dried tomatoes to the empty skillet. Toast 2-3 minutes, stirring often, until the orzo smells nutty.
Pour in the broth, scraping up the browned bits. Add the lemon wheels and drop to medium-low.
Simmer 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the orzo is tender and saucy.
Stir in the squeezed spinach, return the shrimp, and simmer 1-2 minutes just to warm through. Serve hot.

recipes.name: Grilled Chicken Gyro Salad
recipes.blurb: Marinated grilled chicken thighs over a big chopped Greek salad with real tzatziki. Grill-based, so the kitchen stays cool.

items: 1.5 tsp kosher salt, 1/2 tsp black pepper

directions: Combine all marinade ingredients in a large freezer bag. Add all 4.5 lb of chicken and coat evenly. Marinate 20 minutes minimum, up to 24 hours — do it in the morning if you can.

Tzatziki: quarter one cucumber lengthwise, cut away the seedy core, then grate onto a clean dish towel and wring it out hard. Watery cucumber is what ruins tzatziki. Mix with yogurt, lemon juice, vinegar, dill, garlic, salt and pepper. Chill.
Arrange romaine, red onion, tomatoes and chopped cucumber on a big platter. Toss the sliced onion with a splash of lemon juice first to mellow its bite.
Grill on high — about 5 minutes on the first side until dark lines appear, then 3 minutes more. Work in batches; crowding steams the chicken instead of charring it.
Rest the chicken while you toast the pitas on the grill.
Slice chicken thinly. Reserve about 1.5 lb in a sealed container for Wednesday before it hits the table — it will disappear otherwise.
Serve platter-style and let everyone build their own.

recipes.name: Mediterranean Chicken Bowls
recipes.blurb: The payoff night. Monday's grilled chicken comes back in a completely different format — no protein to cook, so this is basically rice plus assembly.

items: ~1.5 lb grilled chicken from Monday, chopped
1/4 red onion, thinly sliced (left from Monday)
1 cup plain Greek yogurt (from Monday's tub)

directions: Start the rice first — everything else takes less time than it does.
Stir together the yogurt, lemon juice, garlic powder, dried dill and salt. Refrigerate until you serve. If Monday's tzatziki is still good, use that instead and skip this entirely.
Halve the grape tomatoes, cut the cucumber into quarter-rounds, thinly slice the red onion, chop the parsley.
Chop Monday's chicken. Warm it gently in a dry skillet for 2-3 minutes — don't microwave it hard or it goes tough. It's also genuinely good cold in August.
Build bowls: rice, then chicken, then tomatoes, cucumber, onion, parsley.
Drizzle generously with the yogurt sauce and finish with crumbled feta.

recipes.name: Shakshuka with Feta
recipes.blurb: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato-pepper sauce, scooped up with warm pita. Vegetarian night that eats like a real dinner.

items: 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes (leave out and pass at the table for the kids)
3 Tbsp chopped flat-leaf parsley, plus more to finish

directions: Heat oven to 375°F.
Warm the olive oil in your skillet(s) over medium. Add onion, bell pepper and salt. Cook 4-6 minutes until tender and translucent.

Add garlic, tomato paste, cumin, smoked paprika and red pepper flakes. Stir constantly 1-2 minutes until fragrant and the paste darkens a shade — this step is where the depth comes from, don't rush it.
Pour in both cans of tomatoes with their juices and the parsley. Simmer gently 5 minutes. Taste and adjust salt and pepper now — you can't season it properly once the eggs are in.
Turn off the heat. Make ten shallow wells in the sauce and crack one egg into each. Spoon a little sauce over the whites, leaving the yolks exposed. Season the tops.

Transfer to the oven and bake 8-12 minutes. Pull them when the whites are opaque and the yolks have risen slightly but still jiggle when you shake the pan — they carry over out of the oven, and overcooked yolks are the only way to miss here.
Scatter feta and more parsley over the top. Serve straight from the pan with warm pita for scooping.

recipes.name: Blackened Salmon with Zucchini
recipes.blurb: Salmon crusted in homemade Cajun spice and hard-seared until the crust goes dark, with zucchini sautéed in the spiced butter left in the pan.

ingredients.group: Cajun seasoning (double batch — this is the whole mix)

items: 2 1/4 lb salmon, skin removed, cut into 5 portions (~7 oz each)
2 1/2 lb zucchini (about 5 medium), sliced into half-rounds
About 4 cups of Monday's cooked jasmine rice

directions: Stir all the Cajun seasoning spices together in a small bowl.
Cut the salmon into 5 equal portions and coat generously on all sides with the seasoning. Use all of it — a thin dusting will not blacken.
Slice the zucchini into half-rounds and set aside.
Reheat Monday's rice: 4 cups into a saucepan with a splash of water, covered, low heat, ~8 min. Or microwave covered.

Heat the butter and oil in a large skillet over medium-high until foaming. Add the salmon — work in two batches so the pieces are not crowded, or the crust steams instead of searing. Cook 5-7 min per side, until a dark crust forms and the center hits 145°F.
Move the salmon to a plate. Add the zucchini to the same skillet and sauté in the residual spiced butter until tender, 5-6 min. Scrape up the browned bits — that is where the flavor is.
Serve immediately over the rice with lemon wedges. Squeeze the lemon; it is what makes the blackening taste like something instead of just hot.

recipes.name: Bánh Mì Bowls with Pulled Pork
recipes.blurb: Everything good about a bánh mì sandwich, in a bowl: crisped pork over jasmine rice with sweet-sour pickled carrot and cabbage, cool cucumber, a fistful of cilantro and sriracha mayo.

items: About 2 cups shredded green cabbage (the quarter head left from Monday)
~2 lb pulled pork reserved from Monday
About 6 cups cooked jasmine rice from Monday's pot
1 English cucumber, quartered lengthwise and sliced
2 jalapeños, sliced thin — ON THE SIDE
1/2 bunch cilantro, leaves pulled from the stems
2 Tbsp sriracha, plus more to taste

directions: MAKE THE PICKLE AHEAD (Monday night, or at least 30 min before dinner): warm the rice vinegar, sugar, salt and water just until the sugar dissolves. Let it cool. Shred the carrots and cabbage, slice the onion thin, pack into a container, pour the liquid over so everything is submerged. Refrigerate — it only gets better through Thursday.
Reheat the rice: into a large saucepan with a splash of water, covered, low heat, ~10 min, fluffing once. Or microwave covered in two batches.

Crisp the pork — this is the step that makes it a new meal instead of leftovers. Heat a dry large skillet over medium-high. Spread the pork in a single layer and leave it alone 3–4 min until the underside browns and crackles, then toss and repeat once. Work in two batches; a crowded pan steams.
Stir the mayonnaise and sriracha together.
Prep the cold stuff: slice the cucumber into quarter-rounds, slice the jalapeños, pull the cilantro leaves.
Build: ~1 1/2 cups rice per bowl, a generous pile of crisped pork, 1/2 cup of the drained pickle, cucumber, a real handful of cilantro. Zigzag the sriracha mayo over the top.
Jalapeños and extra sriracha stay on the table so everyone dials their own heat.

recipes.name: Cherry Tomato & Summer Squash Pasta with Chicken Sausage
recipes.blurb: Cherry tomatoes roasted until they burst, with zucchini and yellow squash, tossed through whole-grain pasta in a light goat cheese and lemon sauce. Italian chicken sausage added so it actually holds as a dinner.

items: 1 lb whole grain rotini, fusilli or penne
3 medium yellow squash, quartered lengthwise and sliced into 1/4-inch wedges
2 medium zucchini, quartered lengthwise and sliced into 1/4-inch wedges
2 small cloves garlic, pressed or minced
Generous pinch red pepper flakes — ON THE SIDE for the kids' portions
Salt and freshly ground black pepper

directions: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a large baking sheet with parchment. Toss the cherry tomatoes, zucchini and yellow squash with the olive oil, salt and pepper. Spread in a single layer — use two sheets if it looks crowded, because piled vegetables steam instead of roasting. Roast 25 min, stirring halfway, until the tomatoes burst and the squash is tender.
While that roasts, sear the sausage: brown the links in a skillet over medium, 10-12 min, turning, until cooked through. Rest 5 min, then slice into coins on the bias.
Boil a large pot of well-salted water and cook the pasta to al dente per the package. Reserve 1 cup of pasta water before draining, then return the pasta to the pot.

While the pasta is still hot, add the lemon juice, butter, goat cheese, garlic and a pinch of red pepper flakes. Add 1/4 cup of the reserved pasta water and toss gently until everything is coated and glossy. Add more pasta water a splash at a time if it looks tight — the goat cheese is the sauce, so it needs the starch water to loosen.
Add the roasted vegetables and every drop of the juices from the pan, plus the sliced sausage. Toss gently. Taste and correct the salt and pepper.
Top with the chopped basil and serve immediately. Extra red pepper flakes and grated parmesan on the table.

recipes.name: Crispy Oven Pulled Pork with Cabbage Slaw
recipes.blurb: Slow-roasted pork shoulder with a sweet-smoky bark, pulled into a tangy cider mop and piled on rolls with crunchy cabbage-carrot slaw.

ingredients.group: Pork (already rubbed and in the fridge)
items: 6 lb boneless pork shoulder (Boston butt), rubbed 8/23
Rub already applied: kosher salt, brown sugar, smoked paprika, chipotle powder
3/4 head green cabbage, thinly sliced (save the last quarter for Tuesday)
1/3 cup mayonnaise, plus more to taste
Hot sauce on the side — keeps the roast itself mild for the kids

directions: Make the mop: whisk the cider vinegar, ketchup, brown sugar, black pepper and 1/2 cup water until the sugar dissolves. Makes about 2 1/2 cups.
By 12:30 PM: heat oven to 300°F. Unwrap the pork, pour off any accumulated juices, set it in a roasting pan and put it in.

After the first hour, add 1/4 cup of mop to the pan juices and baste. Baste again every hour with whatever has collected in the pan. Roast about 5 hours (a 6 lb roast may want 5 1/2), until the meat collapses and yields easily to a fork.
Let it rest — it can sit at room temperature up to 1 1/2 hours. Shred with two forks, discarding the big chunks of fat. Pour up to 3/4 cup of mop over the shredded meat to season and moisten it.
↻ RESERVE NOW, BEFORE IT HITS THE TABLE: pull about 2 lb of the shredded pork into a container and refrigerate it. That is Tuesday's dinner and it will not survive the table if you leave it out.

Slaw: quarter, core and thinly slice about three quarters of the cabbage (save the rest for Tuesday's pickle). Toss with the shredded carrots and 1/3 cup of the mop, then mix in the mayonnaise. Salt and pepper to taste.

↻ ALSO TONIGHT, while the pork rests: cook 2 cups dry jasmine rice (2 cups rice + 3 cups water, covered, boil then 15 min low, then 15 min off-heat covered). Cool and refrigerate — that is Tuesday's bowl base.
Serve on rolls with slaw and the remaining mop. Hot sauce on the table.

recipes.name: Oven-Baked Fish with Tomatoes, Roasted Broccoli & Lemon-Parsley Orzo
recipes.blurb: White fish baked under a blanket of garlicky fire-roasted tomatoes so it cannot dry out, with broccoli roasted hard on a sheet pan and a bright lemon-parsley orzo alongside.

items: 2 lb white fish fillets — cod, grouper or pollock (eight 4 oz fillets)
2 (14.5 oz) cans fire-roasted diced tomatoes, drained well
2 lb broccoli crowns, cut into florets
2 Tbsp olive oil, salt and pepper

directions: Heat the oven to 400°F. Put a large pot of salted water on for the orzo.
Drain the tomatoes well — wet tomatoes make watery fish. Stir them together with the garlic, 2 Tbsp olive oil, oregano, 1/2 tsp salt, about 10 cranks of pepper and 1 Tbsp lemon juice.

Spread a third of the tomato mixture across the bottom of a 9x13 baking dish. Lay the fish fillets on it in a single layer, not overlapping. Spoon the rest of the tomatoes over the top so the fish is completely covered.
Cut the broccoli into florets and toss with 2 Tbsp olive oil, salt and pepper on a sheet pan. Spread them out cut-side down — that is where the char comes from.
Both go in: fish on the middle rack, broccoli on the upper rack. 15–18 min — fish flakes and reads 145°F, broccoli charred at the edges and still firm at the stem.
Meanwhile boil the orzo 8–9 min, drain, and toss while hot with the butter, the juice of 1 lemon, most of the chopped parsley, and salt and pepper to taste.
Scatter the last of the parsley over the fish. Lemon wedges and red pepper flakes on the table.

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Chicken Tikka
recipes.blurb: Yogurt-and-garam-masala marinated chicken thighs roasted hard on two sheet pans with cauliflower and Yukon potatoes, finished with cucumber raita, lemon-pickled red onion and cilantro.

items: 1 knob fresh ginger, ~2 in, peeled and minced (about 2 Tbsp)
1/4 tsp chili powder or cayenne (kept mild on purpose)
1 1/2 lb Yukon Gold potatoes, cut in 3/4-in chunks
1 English cucumber, grated and squeezed dry
2 Tbsp chopped cilantro, 1/4 tsp ground cumin, pinch salt, squeeze of lemon
1/2 red onion, sliced into thin rings
3 lemons (2 for wedges, 1 for the onion and raita)

directions: Ahead (15 min to 24 hr): mince the ginger, garlic and jalapeño. Whisk into 3/4 cup yogurt with the salt, chili powder, turmeric, cumin, sugar, paprika and garam masala. Coat the chicken thoroughly and refrigerate.
Heat the oven to 425°F. Line two half-sheet pans with foil and rub each with 1 Tbsp olive oil.
Toss the potatoes and cauliflower with the remaining oil, 3/4 tsp salt and the cumin seeds. Divide between the two pans in a single layer — crowding is what keeps them from browning.
Lift the chicken out of the marinade, letting the excess drip off, and nestle the pieces skin-side up among the vegetables.
Roast 20 min. Toss the vegetables, swap the pans top-to-bottom, and roast 15–20 min more (35–40 total) — chicken 175°F at the bone, vegetables browned at the edges.

While it roasts: separate the red onion into rings and toss with a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of salt. Grate the cucumber, wring it out in a towel, and stir into 3/4 cup yogurt with the cilantro, cumin, salt and lemon.
Serve straight from the pans: raita, pickled onion rings, chopped cilantro, lemon wedges. Cayenne or hot sauce on the table for whoever wants it.

recipes.name: Beef & Broccoli Stir-Fry Noodles
recipes.blurb: Thin-sliced sirloin seared hard, broccoli steamed bright in the same pan, tossed with rice noodles in a soy-ginger-chili sauce. Thirty minutes, one wok, everything chopped before the heat goes on. Built on the ad's thin-sliced sirloin tip steak at $9.99/lb.

items: 1 Tbsp chili garlic sauce (plus more at the table)
1 1/2 lb thin-sliced sirloin tip steak, cut across the grain into bite-size strips
1 bunch broccoli, cut into small florets (the second of the two bunches)
4-6 green onions, sliced — whites and greens kept separate
A handful of cilantro, from Monday's bunch

directions: Cook the rice noodles per the package just to al dente. Drain, rinse under cool water so they don't glue together, and set aside.
Whisk the soy sauce, water, brown sugar, chili garlic sauce and sesame oil together. Set the bowl next to the stove.

Prep everything BEFORE the pan gets hot — this cooks too fast to chop as you go. Mince the garlic, grate the ginger and the carrots, slice the green onions into two piles (whites, greens), cut the broccoli into small florets, and slice the beef across the grain.

Heat 1 Tbsp oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high until it shimmers. Sear the beef in TWO batches in a single layer — crowding it steams it grey. 1-2 minutes a side, just to brown; it finishes at the end. Move it to a plate with its juices.
Add the second Tbsp of oil, then the broccoli florets and 3 Tbsp water. Cover and steam 3 minutes, until bright green and barely tender.
Add the garlic, ginger and the white parts of the green onions. Stir-fry 1 minute. Add the grated carrot and go 1 minute more.
Add the noodles, the sauce, and the beef with everything on the plate. Toss until coated and the liquid is absorbed, about 2 minutes.
Off the heat. Top with the green onion tops and torn cilantro. Extra chili garlic sauce on the table.

recipes.name: Chimichurri Grilled Chicken with Roasted Potatoes & Tomato-Cucumber Salad
recipes.blurb: Chicken breasts marinated in yogurt, honey and chimichurri, grilled hard and finished with more raw herb sauce, alongside crisp smoked-paprika potato wedges and a cold tomato-cucumber salad. Built on this week's anchor deal — Perdue boneless skinless chicken breasts, BOGO FREE.

ingredients.group: Chimichurri — DOUBLE BATCH, half of it is Tuesday's dinner
items: 2 cups packed Italian parsley leaves (about 1 large bunch)
1 cup packed cilantro leaves (about half a bunch — the rest goes to Thursday)
1/2 tsp crushed red pepper (leave it out and pass it at the table for the kids)
5 lb boneless skinless chicken breasts (both Perdue BOGO packs)
About 2.5 lb of that is tonight; the rest becomes Wednesday
3 lb russet potatoes, cut into wedges
1 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tsp black pepper, 1 tsp smoked paprika
1 lb Campari tomatoes, quartered (ONE of the two packages)
1 pkg mini cucumbers, sliced (ONE of the two BOGO packages)
2 Tbsp olive oil, juice of 1/2 lemon, salt

directions: SUNDAY NIGHT (or by 3 PM Monday) — make the chimichurri. Pick the parsley and cilantro leaves off the stems and mince them very fine. Mince the garlic. Stir everything together with the olive oil, red wine vinegar, oregano, cumin, red pepper and salt.
↻ SPLIT IT NOW: move half the chimichurri (about 1 cup) into a jar and put it in the back of the fridge. That is TUESDAY'S dinner. If it all gets eaten Monday, Tuesday is just plain rice.
Whisk 1/2 cup of the remaining chimichurri into the Greek yogurt and honey until smooth.

Pat all 5 lb of chicken dry. Pound any breast thicker than about an inch to even thickness. Season all over with the salt and pepper, drop into one or two gallon zip-top bags, pour the yogurt marinade in, seal, squish it around and refrigerate at least 2 hours (overnight is better).

MONDAY — heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the potato wedges with olive oil, salt, pepper and smoked paprika. Spread cut-side down on a sheet pan and roast 35-40 minutes, flipping once, until deeply browned and crisp.

Make the salad while the potatoes roast: quarter ONE package of tomatoes, slice ONE package of cucumbers, shave the red onion, toss with olive oil, lemon juice and salt. ↻ Leave the second package of each sealed in the fridge — that is Wednesday's salad.

Heat the grill to 375-400°F. Wipe most of the marinade off the chicken (the yogurt and honey will burn) and grill the FULL 5 lb — roughly 6-7 minutes a side, until 160°F. Breasts go fast and go dry fast: pull each piece when it hits temperature, not when the clock says so.
Rest the chicken 5 minutes under foil; it carries to 165°F.

↻ RESERVE NOW, BEFORE ANY OF IT REACHES THE TABLE: pull about 2 lb of the grilled chicken aside, chop it into small pieces, and refrigerate in a sealed container. That is Wednesday's quesadilla filling, and it will not survive dinner if you leave it out.
Slice the rest across the grain, spoon the reserved fresh chimichurri over the top, and serve with the potatoes and salad. Crushed red pepper on the side for whoever wants it.

recipes.name: Creamy Chicken & Spinach Quesadillas (Monday's Chicken)
recipes.blurb: Monday's grilled chimichurri chicken chopped into a creamy spinach-and-jack filling, folded into flour tortillas and griddled until crisp, with a cold tomato-cucumber salad on the side. No protein gets cooked tonight. Flour tortillas and shredded cheese are both BOGO this week.

ingredients.group: Filling (uses Monday's chicken — nothing to cook)
items: 2 lb Monday's grilled chimichurri chicken, chopped small (already cooked, in the fridge)
8 oz shredded Monterey jack or Mexican-blend cheese
1 1/2 tsp chili powder, 1/2 tsp cumin, 1/4 tsp garlic powder, 1/2 tsp salt
1 Tbsp cooking oil for the pan
The reserved package of Campari tomatoes, quartered
The reserved package of mini cucumbers, sliced
2 Tbsp olive oil, juice of 1/2 lemon, salt
Pickled jalapeños — heat stays off the plate and on the table

directions: Take the chopped chicken out of the fridge and toss it with the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder and salt. Monday's marinade already seasoned it, so this is a top-up, not a full seasoning — taste before you add more salt.
Roughly chop the spinach. In a large bowl, stir together the chicken, spinach, shredded cheese and sour cream until the filling holds together in a scoop.
Divide the filling among the 8 flour tortillas — about 3/4 cup each, spread over one half — and fold each one closed.

Wipe a large skillet or griddle with oil and set it over medium heat. Cook the quesadillas 3-5 minutes a side, until the tortillas are browned and crisp. Two or three at a time; hold the finished ones on a sheet pan in a 200°F oven so everyone eats hot.
Salad: quarter the reserved tomatoes, slice the reserved cucumbers, toss with the lettuce shreds, olive oil, lemon juice and salt.
Cut each quesadilla in half. Salsa and pickled jalapeños on the side.

recipes.name: One-Pot Lemon Garlic Shrimp & Rice with Monday's Chimichurri
recipes.blurb: Rice toasted in garlic butter, simmered in lemony broth, with two pounds of shrimp steamed right on top in the last five minutes — then Monday's leftover chimichurri spooned over at the table. One pan, one burner. Anchored on Publix shrimp, BOGO FREE.

items: 2 lb raw peeled & deveined shrimp (both BOGO bags), thawed
2 lemons — one juiced (about 3 Tbsp), one sliced for the table
1 1/2 tsp Tony Chachere's or other Cajun seasoning
Monday's reserved chimichurri (about 1 cup, in the jar in the fridge)

directions: Thaw the shrimp if they are still frozen — 10 minutes in a colander under cool running water does it. Pat them dry.
Juice one lemon (about 3 Tbsp) and slice the other for the table. Mince the garlic. Chop the parsley.
Melt the butter in a deep 12-inch skillet over medium heat. Add the garlic and sauté 1-2 minutes, until fragrant but not browned.
Add the rice and sauté 1-2 minutes more, stirring, until it snaps and crackles and smells toasty.
Add the broth, water, lemon juice, Cajun seasoning and parsley. Stir once to combine.
Cover, raise the heat to medium-high and bring to a full boil. Then drop to low and simmer, still covered, for 12 minutes.
Scatter all the shrimp over the surface of the rice in an even layer. Cover again and cook on low 5-6 minutes, until the shrimp are pink and opaque all the way through.
Off the heat, rest covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and stir the shrimp partway in.
↻ Spoon Monday's chimichurri over each bowl at the table — this is the point of the night. It turns a soft, mild lemon rice into something sharp and herby. Lemon slices and hot sauce on the side.

recipes.name: Italian Sausage & Broccoli Pasta
recipes.blurb: No sauce — just farfalle, browned Italian sausage and a pile of fresh broccoli tossed in garlicky chili oil, with smoked gouda melted through it and a hard squeeze of lemon at the table. Chosen off two deals at once: Carando Italian sausage BOGO FREE and Red Apple smoked gouda BOGO FREE.

items: 1 1/2 lb Italian sausage, casings removed (1 1/2 of the two BOGO packs)
1/4 tsp crushed red pepper in the pan — the jar goes on the table
2 bunches broccoli cut into florets, minus the cup Wednesday took (about 1 1/4 lb)
3 oz smoked gouda, grated (Red Apple BOGO)
2 oz shredded parmesan or Italian blend
Salt and black pepper to taste

directions: Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil and cook the farfalle to al dente, 7-10 minutes. ↻ Before you drain it, dip out 1 cup of the pasta water.
While the water heats, mince the garlic and cut the broccoli into bite-sized florets.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium. Garlic for 1-2 minutes, until it smells like something but hasn't browned, then the 1/4 tsp crushed red pepper for another 30 seconds.
Squeeze the sausage out of its casings into the skillet. Break it up with a spatula and cook until browned through, 8-10 minutes.

Add the broccoli, toss it in the sausage fat, and cook 4-5 minutes until it's tender with a little color on it. Fresh broccoli takes longer than the frozen the original recipe uses — give it the time.
Add the drained pasta to the skillet with a splash of the pasta water and toss until every piece is coated in the garlic oil. More pasta water, a splash at a time, if it looks dry.
Off the heat, stir in the smoked gouda and the parmesan so they melt into the pasta rather than seizing. Salt and pepper to taste.
Parsley over the top. Lemon wedges and the red pepper jar on the table — the squeeze of lemon is what keeps this from tasting heavy, so don't skip it.

recipes.name: Pork Fried Rice (Tuesday's pork, Tuesday's rice)
recipes.blurb: The fastest night of the week and the cheapest: Tuesday's cold rice and cold roast pork hit a hot pan with egg, carrot, pepper, broccoli, ginger and garlic. No new protein bought, no protein cooked. Adapted from Budget Bytes' chicken fried rice — same method, Tuesday's already-cooked pork folded in at the end, and broccoli in place of the frozen peas.

items: 4 cups cooked rice, cold from the fridge
About 1 lb cooked pork tenderloin, diced 1/2 inch
1 cup small broccoli florets (cut off one of the 2-for-$6 bunches)
4 green onions, sliced, white ends and green tops kept separate

directions: Prep first, cook second. Dice the carrots, bell pepper and pork; cut the broccoli into small florets; slice the green onions and keep the white ends apart from the green tops; mince the garlic and grate the ginger.
Whisk the eggs. Heat a large nonstick skillet or wok over medium with 2 Tbsp of the cooking oil. Scramble the eggs gently until just set and slide them out onto a plate.

Turn the heat up to medium-high. Carrots first, 2 minutes. Then the bell pepper, broccoli and the white ends of the green onions, 2-3 minutes more, until the broccoli is bright green and barely tender. Move it all onto the plate with the eggs.

Add the last 1 Tbsp of oil. Garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, then the cold rice. Press it flat into the pan and leave it alone for a minute before stirring — that's where the toasted bits come from. About 3 minutes total.
Pour the soy sauce and toasted sesame oil over the rice and stir until the color is even.
Turn the heat OFF, then fold the pork, eggs and vegetables back in. The residual heat is enough to warm the pork through — it's already cooked, and anything more dries it out.
Taste and add soy sauce if it needs it. Green onion tops over the top. Sriracha or chili crisp on the table for whoever wants heat.

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Greek Chicken & Vegetables
recipes.blurb: Chicken breast and a whole sheet pan of peppers, tomatoes and red onion roasted in a lemon-garlic-oregano marinade, finished with kalamata olives, feta and lemon zest, scooped up with warm pita. Built on this week's anchor deal — Publix boneless skinless chicken breasts, BOGO FREE.

ingredients.group: Lemon-garlic marinade — makes extra on purpose
items: 2 lemons — zest one, juice both (about 1/2 cup juice)
3 lb boneless skinless chicken breast (out of the BOGO pack — freeze the rest)
1 lb Campari tomatoes, halved (ONE of the two BOGO packs)
3 bell peppers, cut in 1-1.5 inch pieces
1/2 large red onion, cut in 1-1.5 inch pieces (the other half is Tuesday's salad)
4 oz crumbled feta (half the 8-oz Président BOGO pack)
A good handful of flat-leaf parsley, chopped

directions: Heat the oven to 400°F. Zest one lemon into a small bowl and set that zest aside — it goes on at the very end, not into the marinade. Juice both lemons, about 1/2 cup.

↻ Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper together. POUR 1/3 CUP INTO A JAR NOW and put it in the fridge. That is Tuesday's salad dressing, and this is the only moment you can take it — raw chicken goes in this bowl next.

Cut the bell peppers and half the red onion into 1-1.5 inch pieces and halve the Campari tomatoes. Spread them on a large rimmed sheet pan — use two pans if it looks crowded, because crowded vegetables steam instead of roast. Toss with about half of the marinade that's left. Roast 10 minutes.
While that goes: pound the chicken breasts to an even 1/2-3/4 inch thick and cut each one into two pieces. Toss them in a shallow dish with the rest of the marinade.
Pull the pan out, stir the vegetables, and push them to the edges to open up the middle. Lay the chicken in the center. Back in the oven for 20-25 minutes, until the thickest piece reads 165°F.
Worth the extra five minutes: broil 3-5 minutes at the end for color and a few charred edges.
Scatter the olives, feta, reserved lemon zest and parsley over the whole pan. Warm the pitas and serve straight off the sheet. Whatever chicken is left makes good lunches.

↻ BEFORE BED — marinate Tuesday's pork. It needs 2 hours minimum and overnight is better. Whisk 4 Tbsp dijon, 4 Tbsp soy sauce, 4 Tbsp olive oil, 2 Tbsp brown sugar, 2 minced garlic cloves and plenty of black pepper; pour it over the 3 lb of tenderloin in a zip-top bag and refrigerate.

recipes.name: Soy-Dijon Pork Tenderloin, Rice & Tomato-Cucumber-Feta Salad
recipes.blurb: Two tenderloins marinated overnight in dijon and soy, seared hard and roasted, sliced over rice with a reduced pan sauce, next to a cold tomato-cucumber-feta salad dressed with Monday's reserved lemon-garlic oil. Chosen for the best per-pound protein deal in the ad — Publix extra lean pork loin tenderloins at $4.99/lb.

items: 3 lb pork tenderloin, 2 tenderloins ($4.99/lb this week)
4 Tbsp olive oil for the marinade, plus 2 Tbsp for the pan
Plenty of freshly cracked black pepper
2 1/2 cups dry long-grain white rice (Ben's Original BOGO)
1 lb Campari tomatoes, quartered (the second BOGO pack)
1/2 red onion, sliced paper-thin (Monday's other half)
4 oz feta, crumbled (the rest of the BOGO pack)
Monday's reserved 1/3 cup lemon-garlic dressing, out of the jar

directions: Heat the oven to 400°F. Start the rice: 2 1/2 cups dry rice, 5 cups water, 1 tsp salt. Bring to a boil, cover, drop to low for 18 minutes, then off the heat and left covered 5 more. ↻ This is deliberately double — Wednesday needs 4 cups of it cold.
Lift the pork out of the bag and wipe the excess marinade off it so it sears instead of steams. If you want a deeper sauce, reserve 1/4 cup of the marinade.
Heat 2 Tbsp olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium. Sear the tenderloins about 5 minutes a side until properly browned — one at a time if both won't fit without crowding.
Move the pork to a foil-lined sheet pan and roast 25-30 minutes, until the center reads 145°F.

While it roasts, build the pan sauce in the same skillet: melt the butter, whisk in the dijon and brown sugar (or the reserved marinade), pour in the broth, and simmer over medium, whisking now and then, until it's reduced by half — 15-20 minutes.

Salad: quarter the tomatoes, slice the cucumbers, and cut the red onion as thin as you can get it. Toss with the reserved lemon-garlic dressing, the feta and the parsley. Let it sit while the pork rests — the onion mellows and the tomatoes let go of some juice.
Rest the pork a full 10 minutes, then slice into 1/2-inch medallions. Plate over rice with the pan sauce spooned across, salad alongside.

↻ BEFORE YOU SIT DOWN: set aside about half the sliced pork (roughly 1 lb) and 4 cups of the rice. Spread the rice on a sheet pan or plate so it cools fast, then refrigerate both covered. That is Wednesday's entire dinner, and cold day-old rice is exactly what fried rice needs.

recipes.name: Crispy Pork Carnitas Tacos with Lime Slaw & Pickled Onions
recipes.blurb: Pork shoulder simmered in orange, lime, garlic and cumin until the liquid is gone, then fried in its own fat until the edges crunch. It goes into warm flour tortillas with a sharp cabbage-lime slaw, quick-pickled red onion and feta. Chosen for this week's anchor deal, Publix boneless pork Boston butt at $3.29/lb.

ingredients.group: Carnitas (scaled up from 3 lb to 5 lb; Wednesday needs the surplus)
items: 5 lb boneless pork Boston butt, cut into 2-inch cubes (trim only the thickest fat caps; the fat is what fries it)
1 3/4 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
Water, just enough to barely cover the meat
1/2 cup rice vinegar + 1/2 cup hot water
1/2 head green cabbage, finely shredded (the other half is Wednesday's)
1/2 bunch cilantro, chopped (the rest is Wednesday's)
2 limes: juice of 1 for the slaw, 1 cut into wedges
4 oz feta crumbles (one of the two packs)

directions: Put the cubed pork in your largest Dutch oven or heavy pot (7 qt or bigger; split it between two pots if it's crowded). Add the orange juice, lime juice, crushed garlic, cumin, salt, and enough water to barely cover the meat.
Bring to a boil, then lower to a steady simmer. Simmer UNCOVERED for 2 hours. Don't stir or touch it.

Meanwhile, make the pickled onion: whisk the vinegar, hot water, sugar and salt in a jar until dissolved, add the sliced onion, press it under and leave it on the counter. It's ready in 30 minutes and keeps all week.

After 2 hours, turn the heat to medium-high and boil off the liquid, 45-60 minutes with 5 lb in the pot, stirring and turning the pieces now and then. When the liquid is gone, only rendered pork fat is left.
Let the pork sizzle in that fat until it's browned at the edges, turning gently only as needed; it will want to fall apart, which is fine. Taste and add salt.
↻ SET ASIDE 1 1/4 LB (about 4 packed cups) of the crisped pork in a container and refrigerate it NOW, before anyone serves themselves. That's Wednesday's Cuban sandwiches.
While the pork crisps: toss the shredded cabbage and half the cilantro with the juice of 1 lime and a big pinch of salt. Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet or wrapped in foil in a 300°F oven.
Serve the pork in the tortillas with slaw, pickled onion, feta, lime wedges and the pickled jalapeños on the side. Plan on 3-4 tacos for Paul.

recipes.name: Cuban Sandwiches with Monday's Carnitas & Cabbage-Lime Slaw
recipes.blurb: Tampa's own sandwich: Monday's orange-garlic pork, ham, Gruyère, pickles and mustard, pressed in a buttered skillet until the bread shatters. A big cold cabbage-carrot-cucumber slaw with lime and cilantro goes on the side. No protein is cooked tonight; it rides Monday's $3.29/lb pork plus two BOGO FREE deals, Greenfield uncured ham and Emmi Le Gruyère.

ingredients.group: Sandwiches (6, cut from 2 loaves; Paul gets 2)
items: 2 loaves Publix Cuban bread, each cut into 3 lengths and split
1 1/4 lb of Monday's carnitas (set aside Monday)
8 oz Gruyère, thinly sliced (most of the two Emmi packs)
Dill pickle sandwich slices, 3-4 per sandwich
1/2 head green cabbage, finely shredded (the other half of Monday's)
The rest of the cilantro, chopped
Juice of 2 limes, 2 Tbsp olive oil, 1/2 tsp kosher salt

directions: Make the slaw first so it has a few minutes to soften: toss the cabbage, carrot, cucumber and cilantro with the lime juice, olive oil and salt. Taste and add salt if it needs it.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat. Warm and lightly brown Monday's pork and the ham slices, a couple of minutes per side, then move them to a plate.
Brush the cut sides of the bread with melted butter and toast them cut-side down in the skillet for about 2 minutes, until lightly golden. Work in batches.
Build the sandwiches: pork, then ham, then Gruyère and pickles on the bottom halves. Spread mustard on the top halves and close them up.
Brush the outside of each sandwich, top and bottom, with butter.

Turn the skillet to medium-high. Put in 2 sandwiches, lay a sheet of parchment on top and press them down with a heavy pot or a second skillet, weighted with cans if you need to. Cook 3 minutes a side, until golden and the cheese has melted. Repeat with the rest, keeping the finished ones on a rack in a 250°F oven.
Rest 1 minute, cut on the diagonal and serve with the slaw.

recipes.name: Fall Chicken Sheet Pan with Butternut Squash, Brussels Sprouts & Feta
recipes.blurb: Chicken, butternut squash, Brussels sprouts and red onion roasted hot in smoked paprika, cumin and a pinch of cinnamon, then broiled under feta until it chars. Served over Tuesday's rice. Chosen for Perdue boneless skinless chicken breasts at $4.49/lb; the squash ($1.29/lb) and Brussels sprouts (2 for $5) are on the ad too.

items: 2 1/2 lb boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 medium butternut squash, peeled and diced small (about 3-4 cups)
2 pkg Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved (about 4 cups)
About 6 cups of Tuesday's cooked jasmine rice, to serve

directions: Heat the oven to 425°F with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Mix all the spices and the salt in a small bowl.
Microwave the whole squash for 2-3 minutes so it's easier to peel and cut, then peel and dice it small.

In a large bowl, toss the squash, Brussels sprouts and red onion with 1 1/2 Tbsp olive oil and half the spice mix. Spread them in an even layer across TWO rimmed sheet pans; one pan will steam instead of roast. Roast 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, toss the chicken pieces with the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil and the rest of the spice mix.
Pull the pans, nestle the chicken in among the vegetables and roast another 18-20 minutes, swapping the pans halfway, until the chicken reaches 165°F and the squash is tender.
Scatter the feta over both pans and broil 2-3 minutes, one pan at a time, until it melts and chars at the edges. Watch it closely.
While it broils, reheat Tuesday's rice, covered, in the microwave with a splash of water. Serve the sheet pan over the rice.

recipes.name: Korean Beef Bowls with Sesame Spinach
recipes.blurb: Ground beef browned hard with scallions, garlic and a lot of fresh ginger, then glazed in soy, honey and rice vinegar. It goes over jasmine rice with sesame spinach, crisp cucumber and shredded carrot. Chosen for the Market ground beef 3-lb pack at $4.89/lb.

ingredients.group: Beef (doubled from the 1-lb recipe so Paul is actually full)
items: 2 lb ground beef (from the 3-lb pack; freeze the last pound)
2 bunches green onions, minced (about 2 1/2 cups), divided
1/4 cup minced or finely grated fresh ginger
1/4 tsp crushed red pepper flakes (more on the table)
4 cups dry jasmine rice, a DOUBLE batch (half is Thursday's)
9 oz spinach, plus 1 tsp sesame oil, 1 clove garlic and a pinch of salt
2 cucumbers, thinly sliced (the third is Wednesday's)
Optional: a fried egg per bowl
Gochujang or sriracha, on the side

directions: Start the rice: all 4 cups of jasmine rice, cooked per the bag. It's the only thing that takes longer than 20 minutes.

Brown the beef in your largest skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it into small pieces, about 6-8 minutes. Halfway through, add 2 Tbsp of the soy sauce and two-thirds of the green onions. The 3-lb pack isn't 93% lean like the recipe's, so spoon off the excess fat once it's browned. Stir in the garlic and cook 30 seconds.
In a small bowl, stir together the rice vinegar, honey, ginger, red pepper flakes and the remaining 4 Tbsp soy sauce.

Pour it over the beef and cook 2 minutes, stirring. Take it off the heat, stir in the 2 Tbsp sesame oil and scatter the rest of the green onions over it. Taste; add soy or more sesame oil if it wants it.
Spinach: in a second pan, warm 1 tsp sesame oil with the minced clove of garlic, pile in the spinach with a pinch of salt and toss 1-2 minutes until just wilted. Fry eggs now if you're doing them.
Build the bowls: rice, beef, spinach, cucumber and carrot, then sesame seeds. Gochujang or sriracha on the table.
↻ Spread the leftover rice (about 6 cups) on a sheet pan or wide container to cool fast, then cover and refrigerate. That's Thursday's base.
